name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 partisan lean in a Kentucky open seat
Polymarket prices Democratic win at just 2%
Democrat Melissa Strange raised under $100k with no outside spending
Heavy outside money in the GOP primary, but the seat stays Republican-held
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean and the absence of any competitive general-election signals make this a Republican hold; markets price a Democratic win at roughly 2%. The Democrat's minimal fundraising and lack of outside support leave no evidence to move the forecast.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or a damaged Republican nominee emerging from the expensive primary could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is an open seat after Thomas Massie lost renomination, but the Republican hold on the district itself is not in question. The seat leans Republican by 18 points, and the Democratic nominee, Melissa Strange, has raised under $100,000 with no outside spending on either side of her race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is minimally funded.

Prediction markets give the Democrat about a 2% chance of winning. The expensive Republican primary, in which Ed Gallrein benefited from millions in outside spending, settled the party's nomination; the general election is expected to be a comfortable Republican hold in this heavily Republican district.
